### THE DUPLICATE EMAIL BUG

**Root Cause:** The `PasswordResetWorkflow::execute()` method calls `user_service_.change_password()` which already sends an email notification, then it sends a SECOND email independently.

**Password Reset Flow (SENDS 2 EMAILS):**
```cpp
// File: src/workflow/password_reset_workflow.cpp
void PasswordResetWorkflow::execute(const std::string& user_id, const std::string& new_password) {
    user_service_.change_password(user_id, new_password);  // EMAIL #1 sent here

    // BUG: Duplicate email notification is sent here.
    // user_service_.change_password(user_id, new_password) already sends the notification.
    notification_service_.send_email(user_id, "Password Changed", "Your password has been successfully changed.");  // EMAIL #2
}
```

**Profile Password Update Flow (SENDS 1 EMAIL):**
```cpp
// File: src/service/user_service.cpp
void UserService::change_password(const std::string& user_id, const std::string& new_password) {
    notification_service_.send_email(user_id, "Password Changed", "Your password has been successfully changed.");  // Only 1 email
}
```

### Key Functions

1. **Password Reset Workflow:** `PasswordResetWorkflow::execute(const std::string& user_id, const std::string& new_password)`
2. **User Service Password Change:** `UserService::change_password(const std::string& user_id, const std::string& new_password)`
3. **Email Notification:** `NotificationService::send_email(const std::string& user_id, const std::string& subject, const std::string& body)`

### The Fix

The `PasswordResetWorkflow::execute()` method should remove the duplicate email call. The user service's `change_password()` method already handles email notification, so the workflow should only call:
```cpp
user_service_.change_password(user_id, new_password);
// Remove the redundant: notification_service_.send_email(...);
```

This is confirmed by the test file (`test_008.cpp`) which explicitly expects exactly 1 email to be sent during password reset workflow.
